exampleEn: Belly dancers are known for their ability to skillfully undulate their stomachs.

definitionEn: one-sided
exampleEn: The unilateral decision was deemed unfair by the other party involved.

definitionEn: unfair; not justified
exampleEn: The court’s decision is unjust—he should not go free.

definitionEn: downright, utter, total
exampleEn: My speech was an unmitigated disaster!

definitionEn: completely new and never having happened before; historic
exampleEn: The number of protestors was unprecedented.

definitionEn: to make visible; to reveal
exampleEn: We plan to unveil our plans for the new company project on Sunday.

definitionEn: desire or impulse; to encourage or persuade
exampleEn: He had the urge to tell his parents about his acceptance to Columbia but decided against it. She urged her sister to apply to Stanford.

definitionEn: to prove or declare valid
exampleEn: Your selfish actions do not validate your feelings for me.

definitionEn: ability to be done in a practical or useful way
exampleEn: The viability of the solution is questionable.

definitionEn: urgently necessary
exampleEn: It is vital that you respond by the deadline.

definitionEn: to promise
exampleEn: My brother quickly broke his vow to never eat chocolate again.

definitionEn: to prove to be reasonable
exampleEn: Wanting to look cool in front of your friends doesn’t warrant breaking the law.

definitionEn: production of an amount; to give way to or surrender to; to produce or supply
exampleEn: The farmer’s annual pumpkin yield exceeded 10,000. Cars turning right on red must yield to oncoming traffic. Our experiment yielded many unique-looking vegetables.
